correctness.rationale: On each invariant reflection line the map is a->a+h Delta(a), Delta=sin(2pi/3+2a)-sin(2pi/3-a). Exact two-cycle equations have a unique midpoint m(d) by IFT (Delta'(0)=-3/2). The other equation yields h(d)=4/3+(8/3)d²+(392/45)d⁴+O(d⁶), giving existence and uniqueness above h=4/3. The two invariant tangent eigenlines give return multipliers 1-16d²+O(d⁴) and 1+(224/5)d⁴+O(d⁶); with d²=(3/8)(h-4/3)+O((h-4/3)²), they are 1-6delta+O(delta²) and 1+63delta²/10+O(delta³). Exact symbolic coefficients and seven full-map numerical samples were separately checked; finite tests do not prove all parameters. Exactly six branches are distinct by axis permutation and sign symmetry. No off-axis uniqueness is claimed.

value.rationale: The triangular odd ring is the simplest geometrically frustrated network; its double critical mode makes scalar supercritical flip stability misleading. The theorem determines all six reflection-axis branch realizations and proves they fail to attract on the physical phase-difference quotient, using a nontrivial positive second-order transverse return-multiplier coefficient 63/10. This resolves a concrete local stability question just beyond the known twisted-state sink boundary, without claiming exhaustive attractor classification.
